questions.question: What are methods in Ruby?
questions.title: Methods in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: A method is a reusable block of code: def greet(name); "Hello, #{name}"; end. Ruby returns the last expression by default (implicit return) — no `return` unless you exit early. Arguments: required (a), default (a=1), keyword (name:), splat (*args -> Array), double-splat (**opts -> Hash). Call with or without parens (puts 'hi' or puts('hi')). return exits immediately; without a value, returns nil. Methods end with end. Naming: snake_case; predicates end with ? (empty?), dangerous ones with ! (sort!). Every call returns something (nil if nothing else). Methods are objects' actions (42.even?, 'a'.upcase) — everything is an object, so everything has methods. Define them small and focused; one method, one job.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know def/end, implicit return, argument kinds (required/default/keyword/splat), and ?/! naming.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Adding explicit `return` everywhere (Ruby returns the last expression), or making methods do many things.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Methods: def name(args)...end. Implicit return (last expression). Args: required, default (a=1), keyword (name:), *args, **opts. snake_case; ? predicates; ! dangerous.

sections.title: Reusable Code Blocks
sections.content: A method is a reusable block of code: def greet name; Hello name; end. Ruby returns the last expression by default (implicit return) — no return unless you exit early. Arguments: required (a), default (a 1), keyword (name), splat (star args to Array), double-splat (star star opts to Hash). Call with or without parens (puts hi or puts hi). return exits immediately; without a value, returns nil. Methods end with end. Naming: snake_case; predicates end with ? (empty), dangerous ones with ! (sort bang). Every call returns something (nil if nothing else). Methods are objects' actions (42 dot even, a dot upcase) — everything is an object, so everything has methods. Define them small and focused; one method, one job.

sections.title: Method Anatomy
sections.content:
def name(args)...end. Implicit return. Args: required/default/keyword/*args/**opts. snake_case; ?/! naming.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  D[def greet(name)] --> B[body: last expr = return]
  B --> R[implicit return]
  A[args] --> Re[required a]
  A --> De[default a=1]
  A --> K[keyword name:]
  A --> S[splat *args / **opts]
```

sections.title: Methods
sections.content:
```ruby
# Define a method
def greet(name)
  "Hello, #{name}"      # last expression -> IMPLICIT return
end
greet('Ada')            # 'Hello, Ada'

# Implicit return: no `return` needed
def add(a, b)
  a + b                 # returns a + b
end

# `return` exits EARLY:
def first_even(xs)
  xs.each { |x| return x if x.even? }
  nil
end

# Arguments:
def f(a, b = 1, name:, *args, **opts)
  # a: required; b: default; name: keyword (required);
  # *args: extras -> Array; **opts: keyword extras -> Hash
end

# Call with or without parens:
puts 'hi'
puts('hi')

# Naming: snake_case; ? = predicate (bool); ! = dangerous/mutating
arr.empty?   # ? -> returns true/false
arr.sort!    # ! -> mutates in place

# Everything is an object; methods are its actions:
42.even?           # true
'a'.upcase         # 'A'
[1,2,3].sum        # 6

# Keep methods small; one method, one job.
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Adding explicit `return` everywhere (Ruby returns the last expression).
Making methods long / many-jobs (keep them small; one job each).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: A method is def name(args) ... end; Ruby returns the last expression (implicit return).
`return` exits early; without a value, returns nil.
Args: required (a), default (a=1), keyword (name:), splat (*args), double-splat (**opts).
Call with or without parens; naming: snake_case; ? = predicate, ! = dangerous.
Everything is an object; methods are its actions; keep methods small and focused.
